content.value: The web combines three core technologies: HTML for structure, CSS for presentation, and JavaScript for behavior. Every web site or app runs through a client-server workflow where a browser requests resources from a server and renders content on screen.

A browser parses HTML into the DOM (document object model), computes styles from CSS, and executes JavaScript. If syntax is invalid, the browser often still renders partial output, which is why semantic, consistent markup is crucial for predictable behavior.

questions.question: Which object represents a parsed HTML document in the browser?

sections.title: Web Pages and the Internet Basics

content.value: At a high level, the browser sends HTTP requests to a server, receives responses, and displays HTML, CSS, and JavaScript assets. URLs identify resources, while DNS translates human-readable names to server addresses.

This course is project-driven. Each module builds toward a complete portfolio-ready project: design, styling, interactivity, accessibility, and deployment. Keep notes and draft components as you go so later sections reuse earlier work.

questions.question: What is the browser-first process model for web pages?
options: Load CSS first, then HTML, then JavaScript
Write JavaScript then ask the browser to fetch CSS later
Never need server interaction for any app

content.value: An HTML document starts with a declaration, then an `<html>` root, `<head>` metadata, and `<body>` content. Semantic elements like `<header>`, `<main>`, `<section>`, and `<footer>` improve meaning for browsers and assistive technologies.

questions.question: Which element should contain metadata and not visible page content?

content.value: Core content elements include headings, paragraphs, lists, and hyperlinks. Use descriptive anchor text for usability and SEO rather than vague labels such as
click here.

questions.question: Which anchor text practice is best for accessibility and clarity?
options: Download the Web Accessibility Checklist PDF

content.value: Forms connect users to your app. Choose input types intentionally, use labels linked to controls, and provide helper text for required fields. Client-side validation gives feedback, but server-side validation is still required for trust and security.

questions.question: Which is true about form validation?
options: Client-side validation is enough on its own
Server-side validation should always be part of the flow
Validation should only happen on submit

content.value: Use `alt` text for images and captions or transcripts for media when possible. Iframes can embed external documents and videos but should be used carefully for security and responsive behavior.

questions.question: Which practices improve media accessibility? (Select all that apply)
options: Add descriptive alt text to images
Set width and height attributes only for decorative images

content.value: Selectors target elements; the cascade decides which rule wins when there are conflicts. Inline styles are powerful, while IDs generally outrank classes, and more specific selectors override simpler ones when properties compete.

questions.question: Which selector has the highest specificity in standard CSS order?

content.value: Every element has content, padding, border, and margin. Spacing mistakes in one part of the box model often create many layout bugs, so learn to inspect each layer with developer tools.

questions.question: Which part of the box model is outside the border?

content.value: Flexbox is optimized for one-dimensional layouts. Use `justify-content` for main-axis alignment and `align-items` for cross-axis alignment. Gaps and wrapping help keep layouts flexible when content grows.

questions.question: Flexbox is best for which type of layout?

content.value: Responsive design uses relative units, breakpoints, and progressive enhancement. Start with a mobile-first mindset and expand complexity at wider breakpoints.

questions.question: What is a best practice for responsive development?
options: Design desktop layout first and scale down
Use mobile-first breakpoints and relative units

content.value: JavaScript runs in the browser to make pages interactive. You can store and modify page state, respond to user actions, and update visible content dynamically without full page reloads.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of JavaScript in a webpage?

content.value: Use clear naming, prefer `const` where values do not change, and `let` when reassignment is needed. Functions package behavior, and scope controls where variables are accessible.

questions.question: Which keyword should you prefer for values that do not get reassigned?

content.value: The DOM API lets code read and update elements. Event listeners such as click, input, and submit connect user interaction to updates. Debouncing and guarding against null nodes are important in real codebases.

questions.question: Which listener is appropriate for handling user typing in an input?

sections.title: Arrays, Objects, and Small UI State

content.value: Store UI state in JavaScript objects or arrays, then render derived values to the DOM. This mindset prepares your work for scalable frameworks later.

questions.question: Which types are commonly used to represent structured UI data? (Select all that apply)

content.value: Accessible pages are usable by more people and more robust overall. Include semantic headings, meaningful link text, keyboard focus styles, and visible state changes for interactive controls.

questions.question: Which is strongest evidence of accessible interaction design?

content.value: Performance begins with fewer requests, smaller assets, and caching. Use image compression, minimize render-blocking resources, and avoid unnecessary scripts to improve Time to First Paint.

questions.question: Which strategy helps first paint performance?
options: Optimize images and defer non-critical scripts

content.value: A polished course project includes a clear file structure, deployment from source control, a stable hosted URL, and production-tested behavior. Write a concise README, list features, and track known limitations.

questions.question: Which item is most important for project handoff?

content.value: In your final project, build a multi-section site with semantic HTML, responsive CSS, and interactive JavaScript. Include at least one form and one data-driven component, then publish a public link and a short reflection on implementation choices.

questions.question: Which elements should a good capstone include? (Select all that apply)
options: A single unstyled page with no interactions
